verses: الٓمٓ
ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ
نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ
مِن قَبْلُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَنزَلَ ٱلْفُرْقَانَ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو ٱنتِقَامٍ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَيْهِ شَىْءٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِنْهُ ءَايَٰتٌ مُّحْكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٌ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنْهُ ٱبْتِغَآءَ ٱلْفِتْنَةِ وَٱبْتِغَآءَ تَأْوِيلِهِۦ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِى ٱلْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلٌّ مِّنْ عِندِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ ٱلنَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ ٱلْمِيعَادَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَن تُغْنِىَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَٰلُهُمْ وَلَآ أَوْلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًٔا وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ ٱلنَّارِ
كَدَأْبِ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَٱللَّهُ شَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ
قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ سَتُغْلَبُونَ وَتُحْشَرُونَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ

قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ ءَايَةٌ فِى فِئَتَيْنِ ٱلْتَقَتَا فِئَةٌ تُقَٰتِلُ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُخْرَىٰ كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُم مِّثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْىَ ٱلْعَيْنِ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ

زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلْبَنِينَ وَٱلْقَنَٰطِيرِ ٱلْمُقَنطَرَةِ مِنَ ٱلذَّهَبِ وَٱلْفِضَّةِ وَٱلْخَيْلِ ٱلْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ وَٱلْحَرْثِ ذَٰلِكَ مَتَٰعُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥ حُسْنُ ٱلْمَـَٔابِ

قُلْ أَؤُنَبِّئُكُم بِخَيْرٍ مِّن ذَٰلِكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّٰتٌ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَأَزْوَٰجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ وَرِضْوَٰنٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلْقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلْمُنفِقِينَ وَٱلْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِٱلْأَسْحَارِ
شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَأُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمِ قَآئِمًۢا بِٱلْقِسْطِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ

إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمُ وَمَا ٱخْتَلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ

فَإِنْ حَآجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِىَ لِلَّهِ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِ وَقُل لِّلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْأُمِّيِّۦنَ ءَأَسْلَمْتُمْ فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوا۟ فَقَدِ ٱهْتَدَوا۟ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلَٰغُ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ نَصِيبًا مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّىٰ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ وَهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ لَن تَمَسَّنَا ٱلنَّارُ إِلَّآ أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ وَغَرَّهُمْ فِى دِينِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَفْتَرُونَ
فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَٰهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ مَٰلِكَ ٱلْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِى ٱلْمُلْكَ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتَنزِعُ ٱلْمُلْكَ مِمَّن تَشَآءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَن تَشَآءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَآءُ بِيَدِكَ ٱلْخَيْرُ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
تُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَىَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَىِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ

لَّا يَتَّخِذِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ أَوْلِيَآءَ مِن دُونِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ فِى شَىْءٍ إِلَّآ أَن تَتَّقُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ تُقَىٰةً وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسَهُۥ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
قُلْ إِن تُخْفُوا۟ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ يَعْلَمْهُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُّحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ مِن سُوٓءٍ تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُۥٓ أَمَدًۢا بَعِيدًا وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسَهُۥ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفٌۢ بِٱلْعِبَادِ
قُلْ إِن كُنتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱللَّهَ فَٱتَّبِعُونِى يُحْبِبْكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
قُلْ أَطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ وَنُوحًا وَءَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَءَالَ عِمْرَٰنَ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
ذُرِّيَّةًۢ بَعْضُهَا مِنۢ بَعْضٍ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّىٓ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ

فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَٰمَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُۥ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ ٱلدُّعَآءِ
فَنَادَتْهُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُوَ قَآئِمٌ يُصَلِّى فِى ٱلْمِحْرَابِ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيَىٰ مُصَدِّقًۢا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَسَيِّدًا وَحَصُورًا وَنَبِيًّا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَٰمٌ وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِىَ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرٌ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَآءُ
قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزًا وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ كَثِيرًا وَسَبِّحْ بِٱلْعَشِىِّ وَٱلْإِبْكَٰرِ
وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَٱصْطَفَىٰكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
يَٰمَرْيَمُ ٱقْنُتِى لِرَبِّكِ وَٱسْجُدِى وَٱرْكَعِى مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ
إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
وَيُعَلِّمُهُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ

وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
وَمُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَجِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ
رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا بِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ وَٱتَّبَعْنَا ٱلرَّسُولَ فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
وَمَكَرُوا۟ وَمَكَرَ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرُ ٱلْمَٰكِرِينَ

إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَىٰٓ إِنِّى مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَىَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَجَاعِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
ذَٰلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ وَٱلذِّكْرِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ

فَمَنْ حَآجَّكَ فِيهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ فَقُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ نَدْعُ أَبْنَآءَنَا وَأَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَنِسَآءَنَا وَنِسَآءَكُمْ وَأَنفُسَنَا وَأَنفُسَكُمْ ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَل لَّعْنَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ
إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَهُوَ ٱلْقَصَصُ ٱلْحَقُّ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ تَعَالَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍۭ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَقُولُوا۟ ٱشْهَدُوا۟ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ
يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِىٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَتِ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةُ وَٱلْإِنجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ
هَٰٓأَنتُمْ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ حَٰجَجْتُمْ فِيمَا لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ فَلِمَ تُحَآجُّونَ فِيمَا لَيْسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
مَا كَانَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا وَلَٰكِن كَانَ حَنِيفًا مُّسْلِمًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
إِنَّ أَوْلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِإِبْرَٰهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَٰذَا ٱلنَّبِىُّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِىُّ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَدَّت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ
يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ
يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُونَ ٱلْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
وَقَالَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَجْهَ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱكْفُرُوٓا۟ ءَاخِرَهُۥ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ

وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِلَّا لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْهُدَىٰ هُدَى ٱللَّهِ أَن يُؤْتَىٰٓ أَحَدٌ مِّثْلَ مَآ أُوتِيتُمْ أَوْ يُحَآجُّوكُمْ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلْفَضْلِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ

وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مَنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَّا يُؤَدِّهِۦٓ إِلَيْكَ إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَآئِمًا ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّۦنَ سَبِيلٌ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِۦ وَٱتَّقَىٰ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَا خَلَٰقَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَا يَنظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ

وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقًا يَلْوُۥنَ أَلْسِنَتَهُم بِٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِتَحْسَبُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُؤْتِيَهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحُكْمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُوا۟ عِبَادًا لِّى مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِن كُونُوا۟ رَبَّٰنِيِّۦنَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ
وَلَا يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَن تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ وَٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ أَرْبَابًا أَيَأْمُرُكُم بِٱلْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيْتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥ قَالَ ءَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمْ إِصْرِى قَالُوٓا۟ أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ فَٱشْهَدُوا۟ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
فَمَن تَوَلَّىٰ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ ٱللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ

قُلْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَٱلْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِىَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ
وَمَن يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمِ دِينًا فَلَن يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
كَيْفَ يَهْدِى ٱللَّهُ قَوْمًا كَفَرُوا۟ بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِهِمْ وَشَهِدُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱلرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتُ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ
خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِهِمْ ثُمَّ ٱزْدَادُوا۟ كُفْرًا لَّن تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلضَّآلُّونَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَمَاتُوا۟ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَن يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِم مِّلْءُ ٱلْأَرْضِ ذَهَبًا وَلَوِ ٱفْتَدَىٰ بِهِۦٓ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
لَن تَنَالُوا۟ ٱلْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ وَمَا تُنفِقُوا۟ مِن شَىْءٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِهِۦ عَلِيمٌ

كُلُّ ٱلطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِلًّا لِّبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ إِلَّا مَا حَرَّمَ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تُنَزَّلَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةُ قُلْ فَأْتُوا۟ بِٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ فَٱتْلُوهَآ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
فَمَنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
قُلْ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ فَٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِى بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ

فِيهِ ءَايَٰتٌۢ بَيِّنَٰتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ ءَامِنًا وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلْبَيْتِ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ عَنِ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلَىٰ مَا تَعْمَلُونَ
قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ تَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا وَأَنتُمْ شُهَدَآءُ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن تُطِيعُوا۟ فَرِيقًا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ يَرُدُّوكُم بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمْ كَٰفِرِينَ
وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ وَأَنتُمْ تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُۥ وَمَن يَعْتَصِم بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِىَ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِۦ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنتُم مُّسْلِمُونَ

وَٱعْتَصِمُوا۟ بِحَبْلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا۟ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنتُمْ أَعْدَآءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُم بِنِعْمَتِهِۦٓ إِخْوَٰنًا وَكُنتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنْهَا كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى ٱلْخَيْرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ كَٱلَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا۟ وَٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتُ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ أَكَفَرْتُم بَعْدَ إِيمَٰنِكُمْ فَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ
وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ٱبْيَضَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ فَفِى رَحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِّلْعَٰلَمِينَ
وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ ٱلْأُمُورُ

كُنتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَوْ ءَامَنَ أَهْلُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَّهُم مِّنْهُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ ٱلْفَٰسِقُونَ
لَن يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلَّآ أَذًى وَإِن يُقَٰتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ

ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ مَا ثُقِفُوٓا۟ إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَحَبْلٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلْأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ
لَيْسُوا۟ سَوَآءً مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أُمَّةٌ قَآئِمَةٌ يَتْلُونَ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيْلِ وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ
يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ ٱلْمُنكَرِ وَيُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
وَمَا يَفْعَلُوا۟ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَن يُكْفَرُوهُ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَن تُغْنِىَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَٰلُهُمْ وَلَآ أَوْلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيْـًٔا وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ

مَثَلُ مَا يُنفِقُونَ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيهَا صِرٌّ أَصَابَتْ حَرْثَ قَوْمٍ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَٰكِنْ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ بِطَانَةً مِّن دُونِكُمْ لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا وَدُّوا۟ مَا عَنِتُّمْ قَدْ بَدَتِ ٱلْبَغْضَآءُ مِنْ أَفْوَٰهِهِمْ وَمَا تُخْفِى صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ

هَٰٓأَنتُمْ أُو۟لَآءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْكِتَٰبِ كُلِّهِۦ وَإِذَا لَقُوكُمْ قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا۟ عَضُّوا۟ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْأَنَامِلَ مِنَ ٱلْغَيْظِ قُلْ مُوتُوا۟ بِغَيْظِكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِن تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُوا۟ بِهَا وَإِن تَصْبِرُوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ
وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقَٰعِدَ لِلْقِتَالِ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
إِذْ هَمَّت طَّآئِفَتَانِ مِنكُمْ أَن تَفْشَلَا وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَلَن يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِثَلَٰثَةِ ءَالَٰفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ مُنزَلِينَ
بَلَىٰٓ إِن تَصْبِرُوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ وَيَأْتُوكُم مِّن فَوْرِهِمْ هَٰذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِخَمْسَةِ ءَالَٰفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ
وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَىٰ لَكُمْ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُم بِهِۦ وَمَا ٱلنَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ فَيَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَآئِبِينَ
لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ
وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَأْكُلُوا۟ ٱلرِّبَوٰٓا۟ أَضْعَٰفًا مُّضَٰعَفَةً وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ
وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ
وَأَطِيعُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
وَسَارِعُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِى ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلْكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلْغَيْظَ وَٱلْعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ

وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَٰحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُوا۟ لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَن يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُوا۟ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَجَنَّٰتٌ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ ٱلْعَٰمِلِينَ
قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ فَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
هَٰذَا بَيَانٌ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
وَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلْأَعْلَوْنَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

إِن يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ ٱلْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِّثْلُهُۥ وَتِلْكَ ٱلْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمْ شُهَدَآءَ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَيَمْحَقَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
وَلَقَدْ كُنتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ ٱلْمَوْتَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَلْقَوْهُ فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ

وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًٔا وَسَيَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ

وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبًا مُّؤَجَّلًا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِۦ مِنْهَا وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِۦ مِنْهَا وَسَنَجْزِى ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِىٍّ قَٰتَلَ مَعَهُۥ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ فَمَا وَهَنُوا۟ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُوا۟ وَمَا ٱسْتَكَانُوا۟ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا ٱغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِىٓ أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
فَـَٔاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَحُسْنَ ثَوَابِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن تُطِيعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ فَتَنقَلِبُوا۟ خَٰسِرِينَ
بَلِ ٱللَّهُ مَوْلَىٰكُمْ وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلنَّٰصِرِينَ
سَنُلْقِى فِى قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلرُّعْبَ بِمَآ أَشْرَكُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِۦ سُلْطَٰنًا وَمَأْوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُۥٓ إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذْنِهِۦ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنَٰزَعْتُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ وَعَصَيْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلْوُۥنَ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدٍ وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِىٓ أُخْرَىٰكُمْ فَأَثَٰبَكُمْ غَمًّۢا بِغَمٍّ لِّكَيْلَا تَحْزَنُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا مَآ أَصَٰبَكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ

ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُّعَاسًا يَغْشَىٰ طَآئِفَةً مِّنكُمْ وَطَآئِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنفُسُهُمْ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيْرَ ٱلْحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ مِن شَىْءٍ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِ يُخْفُونَ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَمْرِ شَىْءٌ مَّا قُتِلْنَا هَٰهُنَا قُل لَّوْ كُنتُمْ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَتْلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمْ وَلِيَبْتَلِىَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا۟ مِنكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْتَقَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسْتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُوا۟ وَلَقَدْ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَكُونُوا۟ كَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَقَالُوا۟ لِإِخْوَٰنِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ أَوْ كَانُوا۟ غُزًّى لَّوْ كَانُوا۟ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُوا۟ وَمَا قُتِلُوا۟ لِيَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَٱللَّهُ يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
وَلَئِن قُتِلْتُمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ
وَلَئِن مُّتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ لَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ

فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لَٱنفَضُّوا۟ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
إِن يَنصُرْكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِن يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَنصُرُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ
وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِىٍّ أَن يَغُلَّ وَمَن يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضْوَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَنۢ بَآءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَأْوَىٰهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ
هُمْ دَرَجَٰتٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ

لَقَدْ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِّنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
أَوَلَمَّآ أَصَٰبَتْكُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أَصَبْتُم مِّثْلَيْهَا قُلْتُمْ أَنَّىٰ هَٰذَا قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
وَمَآ أَصَٰبَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْتَقَى ٱلْجَمْعَانِ فَبِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا۟ وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا۟ قَٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوِ ٱدْفَعُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ لَوْ نَعْلَمُ قِتَالًا لَّٱتَّبَعْنَٰكُمْ هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ مِنْهُمْ لِلْإِيمَٰنِ يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَٰهِهِم مَّا لَيْسَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَكْتُمُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوا۟ لِإِخْوَٰنِهِمْ وَقَعَدُوا۟ لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا مَا قُتِلُوا۟ قُلْ فَٱدْرَءُوا۟ عَنْ أَنفُسِكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمْوَٰتًۢا بَلْ أَحْيَآءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ
فَرِحِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا۟ بِهِم مِّنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلَّا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُوا۟ لِلَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْقَرْحُ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ وَٱتَّقَوْا۟ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ
ٱلَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ ٱلنَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا۟ لَكُمْ فَٱخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَٰنًا وَقَالُوا۟ حَسْبُنَا ٱللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ ٱلْوَكِيلُ
فَٱنقَلَبُوا۟ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ لَّمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوٓءٌ وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ رِضْوَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَظِيمٍ
إِنَّمَا ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَآءَهُۥ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
وَلَا يَحْزُنكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لَن يَضُرُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًٔا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَلَّا يَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ حَظًّا فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلْكُفْرَ بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ لَن يَضُرُّوا۟ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًٔا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّمَا نُمْلِى لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِّأَنفُسِهِمْ إِنَّمَا نُمْلِى لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوٓا۟ إِثْمًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ

مَّا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَىٰ مَآ أَنتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجْتَبِى مِن رُّسُلِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ فَـَٔامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ وَإِن تُؤْمِنُوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ فَلَكُمْ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ

وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ هُوَ خَيْرًا لَّهُم بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَّهُمْ سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَٰثُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
لَّقَدْ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوْلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَآءُ سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا۟ وَقَتْلَهُمُ ٱلْأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا۟ عَذَابَ ٱلْحَرِيقِ
ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ

ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَهِدَ إِلَيْنَآ أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ لِرَسُولٍ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَنَا بِقُرْبَانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ ٱلنَّارُ قُلْ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّن قَبْلِى بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَبِٱلَّذِى قُلْتُمْ فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
فَإِن كَذَّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِّن قَبْلِكَ جَآءُو بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ وَٱلْكِتَٰبِ ٱلْمُنِيرِ

كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ وَمَا ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلْغُرُورِ

لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ أَذًى كَثِيرًا وَإِن تَصْبِرُوا۟ وَتَتَّقُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ ٱلْأُمُورِ

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُۥ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُۥ فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَٱشْتَرَوْا۟ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا فَبِئْسَ مَا يَشْتَرُونَ
لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوا۟ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُوا۟ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا۟ فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّهُم بِمَفَازَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
إِنَّ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱخْتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ لَءَايَٰتٍ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
ٱلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَٰمًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَٰطِلًا سُبْحَٰنَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ ٱلنَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُۥ وَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍ

رَّبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِى لِلْإِيمَٰنِ أَنْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَـَٔامَنَّا رَبَّنَا فَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّـَٔاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ ٱلْأَبْرَارِ
رَبَّنَا وَءَاتِنَا مَا وَعَدتَّنَا عَلَىٰ رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ ٱلْمِيعَادَ

فَٱسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّى لَآ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَٰمِلٍ مِّنكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ بَعْضُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْضٍ فَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ وَأُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِى وَقَٰتَلُوا۟ وَقُتِلُوا۟ لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّٰتٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ثَوَابًا مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ عِندَهُۥ حُسْنُ ٱلثَّوَابِ
لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ
مَتَٰعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْوَىٰهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ ٱلْمِهَادُ
لَٰكِنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتٌ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا نُزُلًا مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِّلْأَبْرَارِ

وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خَٰشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ
يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱصْبِرُوا۟ وَصَابِرُوا۟ وَرَابِطُوا۟ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ

leads.title: Jesus brings clay birds to life
leads.summary: In the Infancy Gospel of Thomas the child Jesus shapes sparrows from clay and makes them fly. The Quran has Jesus fashion birds from clay that become birds by God's permission.

passages.text: (3:49) وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةً لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (5:110) إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِى عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَتِكَ إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ بِرُوحِ ٱلْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِى فَتَنفُخُ فِيهَا فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِى وَتُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِى وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِى وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ عَنكَ إِذْ جِئْتَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ

evidence.text: The Quran adds 'by God's permission' (bi-idhnī), which reframes the miracle theologically. That is a response-type detail.

leads.title: Mary raised in the Temple
leads.summary: The Protevangelium of James has Mary dedicated to the Temple, fed by an angel, and her guardian chosen by a sign. The Quran has Mary's dedication, miraculous provision in the sanctuary, Zechariah as guardian, and lots cast for her care.

passages.text: (3:35) إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّىٓ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ (3:36) فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ (3:37) فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَٰمَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (3:44) ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَٰمَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ وَمَا كُنتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ

Only in The king did not reward me; an engraved word; guardians of the king's life; the king's direst hour (CTH 123 §§21-28): Picture of the king's direst hour: no groom left to harness his horses, the charioteer leaping from the chariot, the chamberlain fleeing, not even a gate-dog left nor an arrow to shoot; The sworn may not say 'the king has not rewarded me; I will withdraw from these oaths'; A follower's loyalty depends on being rewarded; unrewarded, he turns away; 'There is no augury in Jacob, no divination in Israel'; The oath is declared to be an engraved word ('this word shall be an engraved limma for you'); The sworn man with his wife, children and subjects must be watchmen and guardians of the king's life, never guardians or onlookers of evil; The king reproaches the sworn man: when things were hard he was not with him; did the king not escape alone from Niḫriya, stay behind alone at Alatarma?; Curse formula: 'the oath gods shall hunt (pursue) you' (NĪŠ DINGIR.MEŠ parḫeškandu); The vassal and his brothers are ready to die with (for) the king their lord.

Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 25 more.

matches.label: Embezzlement of goods held in trust (the god's goods, war spoils)
matches.note: Misappropriating goods held in trust. CTH 264: who sells the god's goods for himself, and who catches him but hides him, 'both shall die'. units.title: Instructions for temple personnel, the gods' herdsmen, the ordeal and the colophon (CTH 264, KUB 13.4 iv 34-81)
The annunciation and the mission of Jesus

matches.label: Parties to a dispute call down divine punishment on the liar, with their wives and children
matches.note: A self-curse that brings in wives and children: CTH 264 the accused drink from the god's rhyton and say 'if we lied, you, god, pursue us together with our wives and our children' (QADU DAM.MEŠ-NI DUMU.MEŠ-NI); Q 3:61 the mubāhala: 'let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women ... and lay the curse of God on the liars'. The Quran has no drink and no rhyton, and both parties take part.

matches.label: The god's holy word is known to those who know it and unknown to those who do not; who can find out his intentions?
matches.note: Who knows your heart (šag4-zu a-ba mu-un-zu)? Your holy word is known to the one who knows it, not to the one who does not. 3:7: the mutashābihāt, whose taʾwīl none knows but God (and, on one reading, al-rāsikhūna fī l-ʿilm). In both a divine word whose meaning is closed to all but the knowing; Ninĝišzida's is a hymn epithet, the Quran's a statement about its own verses.

matches.note: A riddle: 'conceived by no father, conceived by no mother, the reed came out of the breast of the storm'. evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water (weight 7.7); An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Contest on Mount Carmel: Prophet repairs the ruined altar with twelve stones for the tribes of Jacob; Contest of gods: the god who answers by fire on an unlit sacrifice is God; The prophets of Baal are seized and slaughtered at the brook Kishon; Prophet mocks the silent god: perhaps he is musing, relieving himself, travelling, or asleep and must be woken; Sacrifice and altar drenched with four jars of water three times, filling a trench, before the miracle; The people fall on their faces crying 'YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!'; How a public contest between God's prophet and the king's religious specialists ends [contrast between the texts]; 'How long will you hop between two branches? If YHWH is God, follow him; if Baal, follow him'; A single prophet of YHWH stands against 450 prophets of Baal and 400 of Asherah; How the people respond to the prophet's challenge over Baal [divergence between the texts]; Parable: a slave owned by quarreling partners versus a slave belonging wholly to one man; Prophets of Baal limp-dance around the altar and gash themselves with swords and lances till blood flows; and 9 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Mother vows her (unborn) child to God's service [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Mother names her child with a speech explaining the name (weight 6.8); Mother vows her (unborn) child to God's service (weight 6.8). Pair score 21.4.

Only in Hannah's vow and Samuel's birth: Barren favored wife provoked by a fertile rival co-wife; Child brought to the sanctuary once weaned, with sacrifices; Child's name explained as 'asked of God'; A woman's silent prayer, lips moving without voice, is mistaken for drunkenness; Mothers nurse their children two full years; weaning by mutual consultation; wet-nursing permitted; A petitioner calls to God in a hidden, secret voice [divergence between the texts]; Do not be loud in prayer nor too quiet; seek a way between [contrast between the texts]; Mother keeps a vow of silence [divergence between the texts]; Child consecrated as a nazirite from the womb, his hair never to be cut; Remember God within yourself, humbly, without loud speech, morning and evening.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'God is sufficient for us and the best guardian' (hasbuna allah) (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Sennacherib's invasion, blasphemy and the angel's slaughter: An angel of God annihilates the besieging Assyrian army; The enemy king writes letters reviling the God of Israel; Besieger mocks the king for removing high places and commanding worship at one altar; Enemies speak of Israel's God as of the gods of the nations, the work of human hands; King and prophet pray together and cry to heaven against the invader; Defenders stop up the springs and streams so the besieger will find no water; Enemy envoys shout in Judean to the people on the wall to terrify them; Leader contrasts the enemy's 'arm of flesh' with God who fights for us; After deliverance many bring gifts to God in Jerusalem and to the king; 'Do not fear, for those with us are more than those with them'; Enemy king is murdered by his own sons while worshipping in his god's temple; King rebuilds the broken wall, raises towers and builds another wall outside; and 1 more.

leads.title: Elijah taken up in the whirlwind ↔ The annunciation and the mission of Jesus
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Prophet is taken up alive to heaven in a whirlwind (weight 7.3); Seventh ancestor walks with God and is taken without dying (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.7.

Only in Elijah taken up in the whirlwind: Disciple asks for a double portion (pi shnayim) of the master's spirit, granted if he sees him taken; Prophet rolls up his mantle, strikes the Jordan, and the waters divide so they cross on dry ground; Fifty men search three days for the ascended prophet, fearing the spirit dropped him on a mountain or valley, but do not find him; Guild prophets at each town tell the disciple 'today God takes your master'; he answers 'I know, be silent'; Successor picks up the master's fallen mantle and repeats his miracle, striking the waters; Successor strikes the water crying 'Where is YHWH, the God of Elijah?'; A chariot of fire and horses of fire separate the two prophets; The sage lets the prophet accompany him on condition he asks nothing until told; Firstborn of the unloved wife keeps the double portion; Cry 'My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!' at the prophet's departure; Prophet thrice tells his disciple 'stay here', and the disciple swears thrice not to leave him; Some of the spirit on the leader is taken and placed on others; and 3 more.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Something (a reed) born without father or mother, out of the storm [divergence between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; To prove the truth, the parties call down destruction or curse on the liar together with wives and children; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; By whose power a healer revives the dead and heals the sick [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

تُولِجُ ٱلَّيْلَ فِى ٱلنَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِى ٱلَّيْلِ وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلْحَىَّ مِنَ ٱلْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَيِّتَ مِنَ ٱلْحَىِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ

leads.title: Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness ↔ Owner of sovereignty
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Most High rules the kingdom of men, gives it to whom he wills and sets over it the lowliest of men (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the great tree dream and his madness: The sentence is 'by the decree of the watchers and the word of the holy ones'; The king boasts 'Is not this great Babylon which I have built by my might?'; The king's reason returns when he lifts his eyes to heaven and he is restored to his throne after praising God; The seer is dismayed and terrified when he grasps the meaning of the dream; 'Seven times' (periods) pass over the punished king; The felled tree's stump is left in the earth bound with a band of iron and bronze; While the words are still in his mouth a voice falls from heaven pronouncing the king's sentence; A 'watcher' ('ir), a holy one, descends from heaven and decrees the judgment; Take alms from their wealth to purify them; the prophet's prayer is a comfort to them; Advice to break off sins by righteousness/almsgiving (tsidqah) and iniquities by mercy to the poor; Dream of an immense tree whose top reaches heaven, visible to the ends of the earth, sheltering beasts and birds; A king is driven from human society to live with beasts, eating grass like oxen, wet with dew, with hair like eagles' feathers and nails like birds' claws; and 7 more.

Only in Owner of sovereignty: On the day each soul finds what good and evil it did present before it, wishing a far distance from its evil; Believers may not take unbelievers as allies, unless guarding against them (tuqat); God warns you of himself (yuhadhdhirukum allahu nafsahu); God makes night enter day and day night, brings the living from the dead and the dead from the living; O God, owner of sovereignty, you give it to whom you will and take it from whom you will; you exalt and abase; A deity holds paired powers of reversal: raising some and lowering others, turning light and darkness into each other; A deity holds paired powers of reversal: raising some and lowering others, turning light and darkness into each other [divergence between the texts]; The deity turns day into night (darkness into light) [divergence between the texts]; God changes times and seasons, deposes kings and sets up kings; God gives justice to the poor and seats kings (or the lowly) on the throne; The god changes the length of day and night (shortens days, lengthens nights; makes night enter into day); The deity gives the crown and kingship and raises one and lowers another (litany addressed to the deity); and 5 more.

leads.title: Daniel in the lions' den ↔ Torah, Gospel and the clear and ambiguous verses
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Israel's God is called 'the living God, enduring forever, whose kingdom shall never be destroyed' (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Daniel in the lions' den: The accusers, with their wives and children, are thrown to the lions and crushed before they reach the bottom; For thirty days no one may petition any god or man except the king; Darius the Mede receives the kingdom at age sixty-two; A stone is placed on the mouth of the pit and sealed with the king's signet and those of his nobles; A royal decree written by the law of the Medes and Persians cannot be revoked, even by the king; The king spends a sleepless night fasting, without entertainment, worrying over the hero; The pious kneels on his knees to pray; The faithful prays facing Jerusalem through open windows; Rivals can find no fault in the hero except in the matter of the law of his God; The king appoints 120 satraps over the kingdom with three presidents above them, one of them the hero; The hero is thrown into a pit of lions; God sends his angel and shuts the lions' mouths so they do not harm the innocent; and 8 more.

Only in Torah, Gospel and the clear and ambiguous verses: Scripture has decisive verses (muhkamat), the mother of the book, and ambiguous ones (mutashabihat) whose interpretation God knows; God shapes you in the wombs as he wills; The god's holy word is known to those who know it and unknown to those who do not; who can find out his intentions?; God sent down the Torah (al-Tawrat) and the Gospel (al-Injil) before as guidance; God is king or master of the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din); Prayer that God not turn (incline) the petitioner's heart aside, but toward his way; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); The secret things belong to God; the revealed things to us and our children; God formed the kidneys and wove (knit) the speaker in his mother's womb; A surah opens with isolated letters (huruf muqatta'at) of unexplained meaning, e.g. alif-lam-mim.

leads.title: Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings ↔ The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Debts of a foreigner may still be exacted though a brother's are released (weight 7.7); Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [response between the texts] (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Release of debts, release of Hebrew slaves, firstlings: Base thought refusing a loan as the release year nears; the poor man cries to God against you; There will be no poor among you, yet the poor will never cease from the land; Seventh-year release (shemittah) of debts owed by a fellow Israelite; Slave who loves his master has his ear pierced with an awl at the door and serves forever; Firstborn male of herd and flock consecrated to God, not worked or shorn; Freed slave must not be sent away empty-handed but furnished from flock, threshing floor and winepress; Blood is the life; do not eat it but pour it on the ground like water; Firstborn male of herd and flock consecrated to God, not worked or shorn [contrast between the texts]; Open your hand wide to the poor brother; do not harden your heart or shut your hand; Hebrew slaves are released in the seventh year; Relief of debtors: release or respite [divergence between the texts]; Sabbath grounded in the memory of slavery in Egypt; and 1 more.

Only in The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian: Some People of the Book plot to believe at the start of the day and disbelieve at its end; Claim 'there is no obligation on us concerning the unlettered (ummiyyin)'; No human given book and prophethood would tell people to be his servants instead of God's; Argument: Torah and Gospel were revealed only after Abraham, so he cannot be Jew or Christian; Some People of the Book return a heap of gold entrusted; others not even a dinar; Some twist their tongues with the book so you think it is from the book; Abraham's relation to the law given later at Sinai [response between the texts]; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; A word of the root ḥ-n-p (Canaanite ḥanpa 'impious deed', Arabic ḥanīf) applied to a deed or a person [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Abraham was a hanif, neither Jew nor Christian nor polytheist.

leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in The angel sent ahead and promises of conquest: The promised borders run from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines and to the River; Obedience is rewarded with health, fertility and full lifespan; Enemies driven out little by little lest wild beasts multiply; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; God sends an angel ahead of Israel who bears God's name; God sends the hornet to drive out the inhabitants; Make no covenant with the inhabitants or their gods, who would be a snare; God sends terror ahead to panic the enemies.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in New tablets, the attributes of mercy and the ritual decalogue: God promises no one will covet the land while the men go up on pilgrimage; The Sabbath must be kept even in plowing and harvest time; What the tablets given at Sinai contain [divergence between the texts]; Israel must tear down the standing stones of the Canaanite gods; A firstborn donkey is redeemed with a lamb or its neck is broken; God passes by and proclaims his name and attributes of mercy; Whether one person (kin, descendants) bears another's sin [contrast between the texts]; Do not offer sacrificial blood with leavened bread; fat not left until morning; No one shall appear before God empty-handed; The prophet intercedes for the people, arguing from God's reputation; How far God's mercy and his punishment extend [divergence between the texts]; Moses hews a second pair of tablets to replace the broken ones; and 21 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Muteness imposed as a sign [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); God makes the prophet's tongue cleave to his palate so he is mute except when God speaks (weight 7.3). Pair score 15.1.

Only in Ezekiel appointed watchman; bound and struck dumb in his house: The glory seen by the river appears again to the prophet in a valley/plain; The prophet is told to shut himself in his house; If the watchman fails to warn the wicked, God requires their blood from him; Israel called 'a rebellious house' (beit meri); A righteous man who turns to iniquity dies and his former righteousness is not remembered; A spirit enters the prophet and sets him on his feet; The prophet sees 'the likeness of the glory of YHWH' as radiant fire enthroned; 'The hand of YHWH was upon' the prophet, bringing a vision or transport; God appoints the prophet as a watchman (tsofeh) for the house of Israel; The prophet must speak 'whether they hear or refuse'; The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good tidings and warner; The prophet falls on his face at the sight of the divine glory; and 1 more.

Only in The family of Imran, Mary and Zechariah: Angels call to Zechariah while he stands praying in the sanctuary, announcing John (Yahya); John (Yahya) foretold as noble, chaste (hasur) and a prophet, confirming a word from God; Angels tell Mary that God chose and purified her above the women of the worlds; Mother names her daughter Mary and commits her and her offspring to God's protection from the accursed Satan; Mother who vowed her unborn child finds she has borne a girl: 'the male is not like the female'; Sign given to the doubting father: he will not speak to people for three days except by gestures; Zechariah is made Mary's guardian; Prophet promises a childless woman with an old husband a son 'at this season next year'; God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds; Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age [divergence between the texts]; The family of Amram / Imran and Miriam / Maryam [divergence between the texts]; A mother commits her child to her god's keeping, against sin or against the evil one; and 15 more.

matches.label: Doubt voiced at the promise of a son in old age
matches.note: Gen 18:12 wa-ttiṣḥaq śārâ bĕ-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê bĕlōtî hāyĕtâ llî ʿednâ wa-ʾdōnî zāqēn: the old wife doubts and laughs, citing her own age and her husband's; Q 3:40 qāla rabbi annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun wa-qad balaghaniya l-kibaru wa-mraʾatī ʿāqirun: the old husband objects, citing his age and his wife's barrenness. Shared motifs, rarest first: The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be' (weight 7.7); Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils (weight 6.1); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 5.2). Only in Second creation account, Eden, and the making of woman: Eating the forbidden fruit is threatened with death; The first human is put in the garden to work and guard it; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Whether the first couple were naked or clothed before the fall [contrast between the texts]; The first man and the names of the creatures [divergence between the texts]; How the first human's mate is made from the first human [divergence between the texts]; Whether any fruit in the Garden is forbidden [contrast between the texts]; The tree forbidden to the first humans [divergence between the texts]; Four rivers in the Garden [divergence between the texts]; The garden given to the first humans to live and eat in [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; Man leaves father and mother and cleaves to his wife; they become one flesh; and 18 more.

matches.note: Gen 2:7, 19 wa-yyîṣer YHWH ʾĕlōhîm ʾet hā-ʾādām ʿāpār min hā-ʾădāmâ wa-yyippaḥ bĕ-ʾappāyw nišmat ḥayyîm ... wa-yyiṣer ... min hā-ʾădāmâ ... kol ʿôp ha-ššāmayim: God forms man and the birds from the ground and breathes life into man; Q 3:49 annī akhluqu lakum mina ṭ-ṭīni ka-hayʾati ṭ-ṭayri fa-anfukhu fīhi fa-yakūnu ṭayran bi-idhni llāh: Jesus shapes birds from clay and breathes into them, and they become birds 'by God's leave'. The creator's two acts in Genesis, forming from earth and breathing in (nāpaḥ / nafakha, cognate), are done by Jesus, with God's permission stated.

leads.title: Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty ↔ The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 answers the other.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Abraham's relation to the law given later at Sinai [response between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty: God forbids the patriarch to go down to Egypt in a famine; King looking through a window sees the couple embracing and learns they are married; Successive wells named for strife (Esek, Sitnah) and finally room (Rehoboth); Enemies stop up the patriarch's wells with earth out of envy; Whether Abraham had a written revelation, or kept God's laws unwritten [divergence between the texts]; Abraham kept God's charge, commandments, statutes and laws (torot) before Sinai; Patriarch reaps a hundredfold in one year; Seven ewe lambs given as witness to a well-ownership oath (Beersheba); Dispute over a well resolved by an oath-treaty with a local king; The foreign king rebukes the patriarch for the deception; Patriarch passes off his beautiful wife as his sister in a foreign court; Patriarch builds an altar where God appeared to him; and 6 more.

Only in The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian: Some People of the Book plot to believe at the start of the day and disbelieve at its end; Claim 'there is no obligation on us concerning the unlettered (ummiyyin)'; No human given book and prophethood would tell people to be his servants instead of God's; Argument: Torah and Gospel were revealed only after Abraham, so he cannot be Jew or Christian; Some People of the Book return a heap of gold entrusted; others not even a dinar; Some twist their tongues with the book so you think it is from the book; Call to the People of the Book to a common word: worship none but God and take none as lords besides him; Debts of a foreigner may still be exacted though a brother's are released; A word of the root ḥ-n-p (Canaanite ḥanpa 'impious deed', Arabic ḥanīf) applied to a deed or a person [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Whether obligations differ toward insiders and outsiders [response between the texts]; Abraham was a hanif, neither Jew nor Christian nor polytheist.

leads.finding: Abraham's relation to the law given later at Sinai

units.title: Isaac in Gerar, the wife-sister episode, wells and treaty
The common word; Abraham neither Jew nor Christian

matches.label: Abraham's relation to the law given later at Sinai
matches.note: Gen 26:5 ʿēqeb ʾăšer šāmaʿ ʾabrāhām bĕ-qōlî wa-yyišmōr mišmartî miṣwōtay ḥuqqôtay wĕ-tôrōtāy: Abraham kept God's commandments, statutes and torot, before Sinai; Q 3:65, 67 lima tuḥājjūna fī ibrāhīma wa-mā unzilati t-tawrātu wa-l-injīlu illā min baʿdihi ... mā kāna ibrāhīmu yahūdiyyan wa-lā naṣrāniyyan wa-lākin kāna ḥanīfan musliman: the Torah was sent down after Abraham, so he was neither Jew nor Christian but a ḥanīf. Genesis has Abraham keep torot before the Torah; the Quran makes the late date of the Torah the proof that he belonged to neither later community. cf. Jubilees and rabbinic readings of Gen 26:5 (Abraham kept the whole Torah).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'Our Lord, you have not created this in vain' (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Cyrus the anointed; I form light and create darkness; the potter; every knee shall bow: God names and girds the foreign king though he does not know God, for the sake of Israel; God calls the foreign king Cyrus 'his anointed' (meshiho), whose right hand he grasps to subdue nations; God's anointed conqueror will build God's city and free the exiles without price or reward; God did not create the earth as a chaos (tohu) but formed it to be inhabited; God goes before his chosen conqueror, levelling heights, breaking bronze doors and cutting iron bars, opening gates that will not be shut; 'I did not speak in secret, in a land of darkness; I did not say to Jacob seek me in vain (tohu)'; 'Drip, heavens, from above, and let the skies rain righteousness; let the earth open and salvation sprout'; 'Truly you are a God who hides himself (El mistatter), O God of Israel, the Savior'; Egypt, Cush and the tall Sabeans come over in chains and bow to Israel, saying 'Surely God is with you, there is no other'; God gives the conqueror 'treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places'; 'Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God and there is no other'; Woe to him who says to a father 'What are you begetting?' or to a woman 'With what are you in labor?'; and 16 more.

Only in Signs for people of understanding; closing prayer: 'We heard a caller calling to faith: believe in your Lord'; God does not waste the work of any worker, male or female; you are of one another; Be patient, vie in patience, stand guard (rabitu); The heavens recount God's glory; day to day pours out speech without words or voice; Among the People of the Book an upright community recites God's signs through the night and prostrates; Meditate on the book of the Torah day and night; it shall not depart from your mouth; Those who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides and reflect on creation; Catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

leads.title: Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign ↔ The annunciation and the mission of Jesus

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Sign: the young woman ('almah) is pregnant and will bear a son and call his name Immanuel ('God with us') (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in Ahaz, the Syro-Ephraimite threat and the Immanuel sign: The child will eat curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil and choose good; 'If you do not believe (ta'aminu) you will not be established (te'amenu)': faith as condition of survival; God will whistle for the fly of Egypt and the bee of Assyria to settle in the land; God will shave head, 'hair of the feet' and beard with a razor hired beyond the River (the king of Assyria); King invited to ask any sign 'deep as Sheol or high as heaven' refuses, saying he will not test God; Cultivated land worth a thousand silver reverts to briers and thorns (shamir va-shayit), fit only for grazing and hunting; Enemy kings dismissed as two smoldering stumps of firebrands; Aram (Rezin) and Israel (Pekah) ally to attack Jerusalem and install a puppet king (son of Tabeel); A divine messenger announces a son to a virgin untouched by any man [divergence between the texts]; Before a child knows to refuse evil and choose good (or say 'father, mother') the enemy kings' lands will be deserted; Prophet meets the king at the conduit of the upper pool on the highway of the Fuller's Field; Prophet's child bears a symbolic name that is itself an oracle (Shear-yashuv, Maher-shalal-hash-baz); and 1 more.

Only in The annunciation and the mission of Jesus: Jesus comes confirming the Torah and making lawful some of what was forbidden; God says to Jesus 'I will take you (mutawaffika) and raise you to myself and purify you'; Jesus tells people what they eat and store in their houses; Jesus announced as a word (kalima) from God, named the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary; Something (a reed) born without father or mother, out of the storm [divergence between the texts]; Forming a creature from earth and breathing life into it [divergence between the texts]; They plotted, and God plotted; God is the best of plotters; To prove the truth, the parties call down destruction or curse on the liar together with wives and children; The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam, created from dust by 'Be'; Jesus will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity; Challenge to mutual imprecation (mubahala): gather sons, women and selves and invoke God's curse on the liars; By whose power a healer revives the dead and heals the sick [divergence between the texts]; and 14 more.

Only in Covenant curses, exile, and remembered covenant: Curse: your corpses will be heaped on the corpses of your idols; Punishments escalate sevenfold each time the people do not listen; Curse of consumption and fever that waste the eyes and the soul; Curse: you will flee though no one pursues, chased by the sound of a driven leaf; Curse: God will not smell the pleasing odor of their offerings; God answers the people's 'walking contrary' (qeri) by walking contrary to them; Curse: the sky like iron and the earth like bronze; Curse: ten women bake bread in one oven and it is doled out by weight; While the people are in exile, the desolate land makes up its missed sabbath years; The people's 'uncircumcised heart' must be humbled [divergence between the texts]; God remembers his covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham even in exile; The 'uncircumcised' or covered heart [divergence between the texts]; and 6 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The heavens recount God's glory; day to day pours out speech without words or voice (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Psalm 19 - the heavens declare; the Torah is perfect: God has set a tent for the sun in the heavens; The Torah of YHWH is perfect, restoring the soul; its precepts make wise, gladden the heart, enlighten the eyes; 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before you, my Rock and Redeemer'; Prayer to be cleansed of hidden and unwitting faults (shegi'ot, nistarot); God's judgments are more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb; The seven heavens, the earth and everything in them glorify God, though humans do not understand their praise; The sun comes forth like a bridegroom from his chamber and rejoices like a strong man to run his course; Sun and moon each swim in an orbit (falak); God called the Rock (tsur); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters; Superscription 'for the leader/choirmaster' (lamenatseah).

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Those killed for God's sake [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Explaining a military defeat of God's people [contrast between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 15.5.

Only in Psalm 44 - national lament; why do you sleep, O Lord: Our fathers told us what you did in their days: you dispossessed nations and planted them; God made his people a byword (mashal) among nations, a shaking of the head among peoples; God crushed them in the place of jackals (tannim) and covered them with deep darkness; For your sake we are killed all day long, counted as sheep for slaughter; All this came upon us though we have not forgotten you nor been false to your covenant; God sold his people for no price and scattered them among the nations; The petitioner addresses God as 'my King and my God'; God knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal; They did not win the land by their sword but by God's right hand, arm and the light of his face; The petitioner spreads out his palms toward God; 'Awake! Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 24 more.

leads.title: Psalm 49 - no man can ransom his brother ↔ The covenant of the prophets and the apostates

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: An earthful of gold would not be accepted as ransom from one who dies unbelieving (weight 6.8); No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly (weight 6.4). Pair score 13.2.

Only in Psalm 49 - no man can ransom his brother: Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; Death shepherds them; When he dies he takes nothing with him; his glory does not go down after him; God will ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol, for he will take me (yiqqaheni); Refrain: man in his pomp does not abide; he is like the beasts that perish; The poet opens his riddle (hidah) and proverb (mashal) to the lyre, addressing all peoples rich and poor; God enlarges and restricts provision for whom he wills; Their graves (qirbam = qivram) are their houses forever, though they named lands after themselves; No man can ransom his brother or give God a ransom (kofer) for him; the redemption of life is too costly [divergence between the texts]; On that day no patron (mawla) can avail his client at all; Qārūn goes out in his finery and the worldly wish for his fortune; Unbelievers enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat; the Fire is their lodging; Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand; and 3 more.

Only in The covenant of the prophets and the apostates: God took the covenant of the prophets to believe in and help a later confirming messenger; All in heavens and earth submit to God willingly or unwillingly; Duty to accept a prophet God will send later [divergence between the texts]; The religion with God is Islam (submission); Those who conceal the revealed signs are cursed by God and by all who curse; Believers make no distinction between any of the prophets (Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus); On the day of wrath people fling their silver into the streets; silver and gold cannot save them; Whether payment may substitute for a life.

Only in Misers, those who called God poor, and the fire-consumed offering: God took the covenant of those given the Book to make it clear to people and not conceal it; Those who said 'God is poor and we are rich' are recorded and will taste the burning; Misers will have what they hoarded hung round their necks as a collar on the Day of Resurrection; Some demand that a messenger bring an offering consumed by fire as his credential; God grants the unbelievers respite only that they may increase in sin; An offering consumed by fire as proof of the true God or messenger [response between the texts]; Fire from heaven falls and consumes the offering, wood, stones, dust and water; God will not leave believers as they are until he separates the bad from the good; Wrongdoers take the deity's delay for indifference; the delay is not a release; What man can live and not see death, or deliver his soul from the hand of Sheol?; A writer reproaches his addressee: the oath I made you swear before the gods you have thrown behind you; Fire comes out from before God and consumes the offering on the altar; and 4 more.

leads.title: Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David ↔ Badr and Uhud
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The sons of Ephraim, armed archers, turned back on the day of battle (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 40 more.

Only in Badr and Uhud: God helped you at Badr when you were weak; The prophet told to be gentle, pardon them and consult them (shawirhum) in the matter; Such days God alternates among people; Defeat came when the believers disputed and disobeyed after seeing what they loved (the spoils); Whoever defrauds (yaghlul) will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection; After distress God sends down security, a drowsiness (nu'as) overcoming a party of the fighters; Even if in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their death-beds; Many a prophet fought alongside many godly men (ribbiyyun) who did not weaken; The slain rejoice with their Lord and are glad for those who have not yet joined them; Those who restrain anger and pardon people; It is Satan who frightens you of his allies; fear me; Do not consume usury doubled and redoubled; and 25 more.

leads.title: Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar ↔ Israel's self-imposed food law and the House at Bakka
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Baca / Bakka on the pilgrims' way or as the House [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Pilgrims passing through the Valley of Baca (weeping/balsam) make it a place of springs (weight 7.7); The House (Kaaba) made a place of return and security for mankind (weight 7.3). Pair score 22.8.

Only in Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar: YHWH God is called a sun (shemesh) and a shield; Soul longs and faints for the courts of YHWH, the living God; Sparrow and swallow find a nest for their young at God's altars; Wish to dwell in God's tent or house forever; A day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; better a doorkeeper than dwell in tents of wickedness; God gives strength to his king and exalts the horn of his anointed (messiah); Pilgrims go from strength to strength until each appears before God in Zion; Genealogy of Korah and his sons; Heading assigns the psalm to a Levitical singer or guild (Jeduthun, Asaph, sons of Korah, Heman, Ethan).

Only in Israel's self-imposed food law and the House at Bakka: The first House appointed for mankind was the one at Bakka, blessed; All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel (Jacob) forbade himself before the Torah; Pilgrimage to the House is a duty to God for whoever is able to find a way; Whether one who takes refuge at the sanctuary is safe [contrast between the texts]; A food taboo of Israel (Jacob) before the Torah [divergence between the texts]; A fugitive grasps the horns of the altar seeking asylum; Israelites do not eat the sciatic sinew (gid ha-nasheh) because of the wrestling; You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love; The Station of Abraham (maqam Ibrahim) at the House taken as a place of prayer; Abraham was a hanif, neither Jew nor Christian nor polytheist.
